title: Fully qualified?
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a four-month placement in a GP practice. Reception staff book patients with you as "the GP trainee".

Mrs Clarke, 52, has come about a breast lump. At the start of the consultation she asks, "Are you a fully qualified GP?"
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Explain that you're a qualified doctor in foundation training.
options.brief: An accurate answer to a direct question.
options.detailed: You are a fully registered doctor, but not a GP or a GP trainee. Explaining your role accurately lets her decide how she wants to proceed. It ranks first.

options.text: Tell her that you are the GP trainee and fully qualified.
options.detailed: You aren't a GP trainee, and saying so gives a false impression of your experience. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Ask reception afterwards to describe you accurately when booking.
options.brief: Prevents the same confusion for other patients.
options.detailed: Booking you as a 'GP trainee' gives patients the wrong impression. Asking reception to change this helps everyone. It ranks third because it doesn't answer Mrs Clarke.

options.text: Offer her the choice of seeing a GP instead.
options.brief: Respects her choice once she knows your role.
options.detailed: Some patients prefer to see a GP for a worrying problem. Offering this, without pressure, respects her autonomy. It ranks second because she needs an honest answer first.

explanation.issue: This tests honesty about your own role and experience when a patient asks directly.
explanation.keyDetails: You are an F2, not a GP trainee. The booking description is misleading. She has a worrying symptom and has asked directly.
explanation.reasoning: [A] answers honestly, [D] respects her choice, and [C] fixes the system. [B] misleads her.
explanation.competing: [A] and [D] belong together. The key puts the honest explanation first because she needs it to make her choice.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, being honest about your experience and role.
